body.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\),
\(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\), and fix the class constants.  For every deterministic
exact design \(X=(X_{st})\), every interior reference path \(z_0\), and
every \(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), consider
the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) in
\texttt{def:fixed-design-induced-experiment}.  Its nearest-design estimator
satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}.
\]
If \(\delta_0<1/2\), the last display is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\).  If in addition
\(B^4>(Sd)^2\), then
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \left[\{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2\right].
\]
Neither bound uses a lower local-modulus condition.

For every fixed admissible \(z_0\) and every
\(\xi\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the conditional law under
\(\mathbb K_\xi\) given the exact design, with its labels, belongs to
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every design,
and \(\theta_{\mathfrak E}=\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 -\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2\mid(X_{st})\right]
 \le C\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
          \vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}\right\}
\]
for almost every design; under \(\delta_0<1/2\), its right side is at most
\(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).  If every cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\)
exactly, the displayed risk is at most
\(C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\), and
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le C\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\vee N^{-\lambda}\}\).
If instead \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every cohort, then
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \left[\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})\right]\le CR_D,
 \qquad R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D.
\]
No converse in terms of \(R_D\) is asserted.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its labelled observed regular
conditional kernel belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for
almost every admissible \(z_0\) under the marginal law of the query, and
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\) there by
\texttt{lem:causal-identification}.  Hence all preceding conditional upper
bounds transfer to \(P\) at those query values and at
\(P(\cdot\mid z_0)\)-almost every exact design; no conditional version at a
null query is selected.
body.justification: The theorem supplies a bounded replicated-response and full-covariance donor product experiment, a single observable nearest-site rule, and an almost-everywhere causal bridge.
body.gap: Donoho's known Gaussian convex experiment and Akhavan et al.'s strong-convexity minimizer problem do not supply this product law, external query geometry, observable-only rule convention, or causal bridge.
body.consumer: The marginal theorem combines its conditional upper mechanism with fixed-query occupancy and explicit global witnesses.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.      \tag{1}
\]
We first work in the deterministic experiment
\(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Fix
\(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.                   \tag{2}
\]
The donor sample is independent of all unit histories, and the histories are independent across \((s,i)\).  Therefore the variables in (2) are conditionally centered and independent across \((s,i)\).  Boundedness gives \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.                       \tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  The definition of \(t_{s\ell}\) and two triangle inequalities give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 &\le \|X_{s,t_s^0}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2
       +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2\\
 &\le \rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
       +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{4}
\]
Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), powers of order \(\lambda\) are subadditive.  Holder continuity and (4) yield
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+
 \|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda+
 \|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.                  \tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, every balanced fold has cardinality at least \(N/3\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\le qC_\Sigma\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.                                     \tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes
\(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expand
\(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the centered sum in (3) and the approximation terms in (5).  Jensen's inequality applied to (6), followed by \((x+y+z)^2\le3(x^2+y^2+z^2)\), gives
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}.                              \tag{7}
\]
The nearest-site construction is a single measurable function of the observed array and \(X\), selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\); hence it is an admissible witness for the first minimax inequality.  When \(\delta_0<1/2\), Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} makes the right side of (7) at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\).

We next prove the deterministic converse.  If two laws \(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\), let
\(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_0\) the error under law one is at least \(\Delta/2\), and on \(A_0^c\) the error under law zero is at least \(\Delta/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.                                  \tag{8}
\]

For the treated-mean channel, keep responses and donors fixed and, under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take independent \(E_{si}\in\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.        \tag{9}
\]
Since \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), a sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) puts every probability in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The target separation is \(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  The Hellinger affinity of the two product event laws equals
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,                                   \tag{10}
\]
because \(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  If \(a_H\) denotes this affinity, Cauchy--Schwarz applied to
\(|p-g|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\) gives
\(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-a_H^2)^{1/2}<1\).  Thus (8) gives risk at least \(cA\).  A common admissible donor law for the prescribed \(\Sigma\) is obtained by taking
\(Z=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}R\), where \(R\) has independent Rademacher coordinates; its standardized fourth moment is \(q^2<B^4\).

For the fixed-design channel set
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda,
\]
with \(a_0>0\) small in terms of \(B,L,d\), and take
\(f_s=q_s/2\), \(g_s=-q_s/2\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} shows that these surfaces are admissible and agree at every design site.  Deterministic zero responses, identical event laws, and identical donors therefore give identical observations, while the targets differ by \(a_0D_X\).  Equation (8) with \(\eta=1\) yields risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel apply Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} under strict interior and fourth-moment slack, choosing its nonzero coordinate in a cohort \(s_0\).  Under both laws use
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),                               \tag{11}
\]
with \(a_1\) small enough for the Holder and boundedness restrictions.  Keep the response and event laws identical.  If \(e\) is the displaced coordinate, the construction in Lemma \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} and ellipticity give
\[
 |z_{1,e}-z_{0,e}|
 =\frac{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
 \ge c_\eta c_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.                            \tag{11a}
\]
Thus the donor product laws have total variation at most \(1-\eta\), while (11)--(11a) separate their targets by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (8) yields risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the maximum of the three lower bounds and using the two-sided characterization in Lemma \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \ge cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.                                     \tag{12}
\]

We now establish the fixed-query bridge.  Fix admissible \(z_0\) and a labelled point
\(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in
\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Let \(\mathcal X\) be the exact-design sigma-field, \(\mathcal H\) the unit-history sigma-field, and \(\mathcal Z\) the donor sigma-field.  By Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}, \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of \(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H\), unit histories are conditionally independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and all required centering, support, covariance, and moment conditions hold.  Consequently, for \(\mathbb K_\xi\)-almost every exact design, the conditional observed law with labels is a member of \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) at its central point \(z=z_0\).  Its target is
\[
 \theta_{\mathfrak E}
 =\sum_s\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0).                              \tag{13}
\]
To verify the global support clause in the deterministic experiment, boundedness gives \(|m_s(X_{st})|\le B\) almost surely.  The density lower bound makes this inequality true Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity extends it to every point of \([0,1]^d\); hence \(\|m_s\|_\infty\le B\).  The last equality in (13) uses Definition \texttt{def:fixed-query-functional}; the same positivity-and-continuity argument ensures that each \(m_s(z_{0s})\), and hence (13), is uniquely determined by the observable law.  Applying (7) conditionally proves the nearest-design bound.  If each design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site conclusions follow from the geometry lemma.

Suppose instead that \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then the reference pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search.  Certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{14}
\]
The bandwidth floor makes the final term no larger than a constant times \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Since \(r=0\), every selected fit has nonnegative weights summing to one.  Holder continuity bounds its approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of (14), while conditional independence of whole unit histories bounds its centered variance by \(CA\).  Donor unbiasedness, projection contraction, and (6) at \(z=z_0\), followed by Jensen's inequality and (14), yield
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 [\{\widehat\tau-\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\}^2
 \mid(X_{st})]\le CR_D.                                       \tag{15}
\]
The last assertion of the geometry lemma gives
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).

Finally fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  Every defining equality or factorization in the panel class holds outside a marginally null query set; the conditional density and conditional mixing assumptions explicitly hold there as well.  Finiteness of cohorts and dates and countability of mixing lags allow intersection of these conull sets.  Hence, for almost every admissible query, the labelled regular conditional point
\(\xi_{z_0}=(\mathbb K_{z_0};\mu(z_0),m,\Sigma(z_0))\) belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi_{z_0};z_0)=\tau(z_0)\) on the same set.  Equations (13)--(15) therefore transfer to the causal conditional kernel for almost every query and almost every exact design.  No decision rule uses the nuisance labels or potential outcomes, and no regular conditional version is selected at a query-null value.
